gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Immich's own minimum is 6 GB of RAM (8 GB recommended), while the Synology DS225+ and DS425+ that ChatGPT picked ship with 2 GB and take at most 6 GB, so those two can never reach Immich's recommended memory, even though ChatGPT sold them next to an 'Immich' option.
standout_why: I compared against the cited rival pages homelabcompass.com (Immich vs Synology Photos) and esp32.co.uk (Synology Photos vs Immich vs PhotoPrism), plus Synology's cited compare and Photos spec pages. Homelabcompass gives no RAM figure at all ('Performance depends on the NAS CPU and RAM') and no prices. It names only the DS923+ and DS1522+. Esp32 quotes Immich's '6 GB minimum, 8 GB recommended' but names no NAS it applies to and gives no prices. Synology's compare page lists 2 GB installed and 6 GB max but says nothing about Immich. Synology's Photos spec page says recognition is 'only supported on certain models' but gives no RAM figure. None of these pages puts Immich's RAM floor next to each box's installed and maximum RAM, and none prices the field from the makers' stores.
decides: This supports keeping two separate picks. Synology DS225+ or DS425+ is the Synology Photos pick. An x86 box with at least 8 GB is the Immich pick: UGREEN DXP2800 at $389.99 or TerraMaster F2-425 Plus at $469.99 on the makers' stores. The DS225+ can run Immich at its 6 GB minimum only after a RAM upgrade, and never at the 8 GB Immich recommends. The DS925+ ships with 4 GB but takes 32 GB, so it can run Immich comfortably after an upgrade. Our page also needs price fixes: the TerraMaster prices are now $469.99 / $539.99, not $599.99 / $779.99, and the DH4300 Plus is $373.99, not $399.99.
